summary: s2.4 gives the culture, dilution, sampling and kanamycin-PBS quench details, and names the instrument and software. The Attune NxT acquisition settings, the background-control strain and the overnight duration are not stated. Each has a defensible default or a manufacturer source, and none changes what the assay measures, so the experiment can proceed with assumptions.

gaps.detail: Optical channels (laser/filter) for sfGFP, mCherry and mTagBFP on the Attune NxT
gaps.why_needed: Each of the three fluorophores must be read in its correct detector. Otherwise the readout is wrong or has spectral overlap.
gaps.resolution: Use BL1 (530/30 nm, 488 nm laser) for sfGFP. Use YL2 (620/15 nm, 561 nm laser) for mCherry. Use VL1 (440/50 nm, 405 nm laser) for mTagBFP. Thermo Fisher's fluorescent protein table lists GFP-type proteins in BL1, mCherry-type proteins in YL2 (620/15) and TagBFP/mTagBFP in VL1 (440/50). The paper does not state the channels, so this is the manufacturer's recommended assignment. The 510/10 BL1 filter from the FP filter kit is optional and was not mentioned in the paper.

gaps.detail: Detector voltages/gains, flow rate, number of events recorded per well, and sampling volume
gaps.why_needed: These determine whether signals are on scale across the 4-log fluorescence range and whether enough cells are counted for a stable geometric mean.
gaps.resolution: Set voltages once on the brightest and the non-fluorescent control samples so that nothing saturates or sits off-scale. Keep them identical for all 96-well plate runs. Use a plate-reader acquisition at a moderate flow rate (e.g. 100–200 µl/min) and record about 10,000 gated events per well. Reading the 202 µl diluted sample is feasible.

gaps.why_needed: The paper says all samples used the same FSC/SSC gate but gives no gate coordinates. The gate defines which events count as E. coli.
gaps.resolution: Draw a single FSC-A/SSC-A bacterial gate on a non-fluorescent control sample, using log scale on the scatter axes. Apply that same gate to every sample in FlowJo. Optionally add an FSC-H/FSC-A singlet gate.

gaps.detail: Background/negative control strain used for background correction and normalisation reference
gaps.why_needed: Fig. 3c shows background-corrected, normalised geometric means. A non-fluorescent control is needed to define background. The main text does not say which control or reference was used.
gaps.resolution: Include E. coli NEB 5-alpha carrying the mScarlet-free p15A CmR backbone control, or a non-fluorescent plasmid-bearing strain. Grow it in the same medium and plate, and process it in the same way. Subtract its geometric mean in each channel as background. The normalisation reference is not given and needs the investigator's choice. This is an analysis step and does not change the raw acquisition.
gaps.source: standard practice; s2.2 and s2.1 (control plasmid description); Results text of https://academic.oup.com/synbio/article/5/1/ysaa010/5869449

gaps.detail: Overnight culture duration and 96-well plate type/sealing
gaps.why_needed: Growth phase at the 200-fold dilution affects expression and fluorophore maturation. Evaporation or poor aeration in 200 µl cultures can bias fluorescence.
gaps.resolution: Incubate for about 16–18 h at 30 °C and 600 rpm in a sterile 96-well flat- or round-bottom plate. Seal with a breathable film or a loose lid. Use 0.5 µl of overnight culture in 100 µl fresh LB-Cm (1:200). Colonies were picked from the transformation spots and each construct was done in 3 biological replicates.

gaps.detail: Shaking speed during the 6 h sub-culture and the kanamycin/PBS stock preparation
gaps.why_needed: The 6 h growth sets the phase of the cells. Kanamycin at 2 mg/ml in PBS is stated as a translation-stopping quench, but the stock preparation is not described.
gaps.resolution: Shake the 6 h sub-culture at 30 °C at 600 rpm, as for the overnight culture. Prepare 2 mg/ml kanamycin in 1× PBS fresh or from a filter-sterilised stock, and add 200 µl per well. Transfer 2 µl of culture into this and mix. Keep the plate at 4 °C or room temperature until acquisition. Hold time and temperature before reading are unspecified, so keep them consistent across wells.

gaps.detail: Post-acquisition processing ('as described in the main text')
gaps.why_needed: This is the deferred method flagged in the paper.
gaps.resolution: The main text says only that mean and standard deviation were calculated from background-corrected and normalised geometric means across three biological repeats, plotted on a log scale (Fig. 3c). The normalisation reference is not specified. Gating and extraction of geometric mean were done in FlowJo V10. The supplementary data zip was not used.

retrieved_details:
From the DNA-BOT open-access article (https://academic.oup.com/synbio/article/5/1/ysaa010/5869449): after DNA-BOT, triplicate colonies per construct were picked from the agar spots into overnight liquid cultures. Fluorescence was measured for sfGFP, mCherry and BFP at the single-cell level. Mean ± SD were derived from background-corrected and normalised geometric means (Fig. 3c), spanning about 4 orders of magnitude. All 88 spots had at least 5 colonies. Host is NEB 5-alpha E. coli with a p15A CmR backbone (25 µg/ml chloramphenicol).

From Thermo Fisher (https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cell-analysis/flow-cytometry/flow-cytometry-learning-center/flow-cytometry-resource-library/flow-cytometry-application-notes/detection-fluorescent-proteins-attune-nxt-flow-cytometer.html): Attune NxT detector assignments are BL1 (530/30) for GFP-type proteins, YL2 (620/15) for mCherry and VL1 (440/50) for TagBFP/mTagBFP. The 561 nm laser is recommended for mCherry. The optional FP filter kit swaps BL1 to 510/10, BL2 to 540/30 and the 555DLP to 525DLP, but it is aimed at GFP/YFP discrimination and was not stated in the paper.
